page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The host is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon W-3235 processor running at 3.3 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs without hyperthreading. It is paired with 56 GB of system RAM, allocating 7.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the instance includes two NVIDIA Turing RTX 5000 GPUs providing a combined total of 32 GB VRAM (16 GB per GPU). Storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB SSD, and baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong performance in GPU-driven machine learning workloads. In large language model inference tests, the dual RTX 5000 setup delivers top-tier prompt processing and text generation throughput for small (135M) and medium (7B) parameter models, achieving 1841.54 prompt tokens per second and 67.32 generation tokens per second on 7B models. On large 70B models, prompt processing drops to an average 16.92 tokens per second due to memory size constraints. System memory performance registers in the top 25% on PassMark Memory (2838.84), though large block memory write bandwidth falls into the lower quartile at 19.55 GB/sec.

General compute and synthetic CPU benchmarks sit consistently in the middle tier. The dedicated Intel Xeon processor records a Geekbench single-core score of 1460.0 and a multi-core score of 6702.0, with PassMark CPU scoring 14005.52. Support for AVX-512 VNNI assists vector calculations, though single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench text processing demonstrate weaker throughput. The instance includes 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires consideration when planning direct external network access.

The hardware composition positions this instance as an effective resource for small to medium deep learning inference, model evaluation, graphics rendering, and computer vision pipelines requiring multi-GPU acceleration without moving to higher-cost enterprise accelerator tiers.
